reason: The rider should help show whether the cord travels with the wiggle; it is also the only offered action.
expectation: I expect the rider to move as the wave passes, though I am unsure whether it will travel along the cord.

effect: The rider shows that the disturbance travels while the cord stays near its place.
reaction: That makes the difference between the wave and the cord satisfyingly clear.
reason: The tension key is the only offered combination and may let me explore how tension affects the waves.
expectation: I expect adjusting the tension to change the cord's motion, though I don't know exactly how.

effect: Adjusting tension and speed produced a repeating two-loop pattern, with a nearly still point between the loops.
reaction: The stationary loops are an intriguing contrast to the travelling wiggle.
reason: The movable bridge is the only offered combination and may prepare the cord to be played like a string.
expectation: I expect the bridge to change the cord's vibrating length, though I don't know what pattern or sound it will produce.

effect: The bridge changes the vibrating length and transfers vibration to the soundbox.
reaction: That connects the visible wave experiment to making sound.
reason: The foot pads are the only offered combination and may help prepare the machine for playing.
expectation: I expect the pads to cushion or stabilize the machine, though their precise purpose is unclear.

effect: The soft feet reduce table buzz without stopping the cord's motion, and the drive is now off for playing.
reaction: The comparison makes the pads' purpose clear.
reason: The plectrum is the only offered combination and should let me play the cord as a string.
expectation: I expect plucking the cord to produce a sound, perhaps affected by the bridge position.

effect: Plucking showed that the soundbox makes the cord easier to hear and that shortening its vibrating length raises the note; the machine can also return to its wave pattern.
reaction: The two-note comparison was a satisfying way to connect the visible motion with sound.

mostWorthwhile.text: Plucking at two bridge positions was most worthwhile: the change in pitch gave the adjustable length a clear purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the soft feet was the least engaging step, though the reduced table buzz explained their purpose.

surprise.text: The rider bobbing in place while the disturbance travelled made the distinction between cord motion and wave motion clear.

arbitrary.text: The soft feet initially felt a little arbitrary because their purpose was unclear, but the result explained it.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the wave-to-sound connection was interesting, though the single available combination at each step left little room for decisions.
